Hi Theo —

Appreciate the forecast, this is exactly the level of detail we need. High-level response and proposal framing below; happy to set a technical ops call to lock in the playbook.

Proposed model (short):
- Baseline (shoulder) reserve: 20 GPUs pinned to your account (guarantees steady throughput and reduces cold-starts).
- Burst policy: automatic autoscale up to 48 GPUs for short windows. Burst consumption draws from a "safetyband credit pool" — we can pre-allocate credits (measured in GPU-hours) that get consumed when you exceed baseline.
- Headroom & throttles: We set soft thresholds at 30 GPUs (notify + prewarm), 36 GPUs (scale up aggressive), 48 GPUs (hard cap); above 48 we apply graceful degradation.
- Billing: baseline charged as reserved monthly fee; bursts billed against credits first, then metered at a discounted burst rate if credits exhaust.

Operational notes:
- Canary plan: reserve a 2-week pilot (8–12 GPUs) for traffic mirroring before full migration.
- Lead time: provisioning for Dedicated (region us-west) is usually 4–6 weeks from signed SOW; expedited options exist for a fee.

I'll attach our Dedicated template with the operational clauses and an example safetyband schedule.

Next steps: set a 60-minute ops working session (SRE + infra + procurement) — proposed times in your sheet?

Theo / team —

Thanks for the procurement list — below is a consolidated proposal that should address most of your questions. If this looks acceptable we'll convert to a SOW + addendum and open a DocuSign.

Commercial / ops proposal (summary):
- Reserved baseline: 20 GPUs (pinned) — availability SLA 99.9% monthly for baseline capacity. Credit schedule: 10% SLA credit for each 1% below target, up to 50% of monthly baseline fee.
- Burst mechanics: automatic autoscale to 48 GPUs with a safetyband credit pool of 1,500 GPU-hours per month. Credits are billed as a monthly amortized line item and carry a 6-month rolling expiry.
- Overage: if credits exhaust, burst usage is billed at the agreed metered burst rate (discount relative to on-demand). We can set a hard cap to throttle at 48 GPUs to prevent runaway spend.
- Observability: we'll provide token-level latency (p95/p99), queue depth metrics, and per-route cost/consumption dashboards via the Redwood Console; SRE alerts can be forwarded to your PagerDuty.
- Lead time & minimums: standard provisioning 4–6 weeks. Minimum commitment: 3 months for pilot, 12 months for production with ramp milestones (we can do a 90-day ramp schedule in the SOW).

Operational guarantees:
- Pre-warm notifications: at 50% of safetyband burn we'll send a proactive alert and recommend prewarm steps.
- Canary: 2-week pilot in a dedicated VLAN with traffic mirroring; we'll assign a Solutions Engineer and an Onboarding PM.

Action items (owners):
- Redwood: draft SOW + addendum, include SLA table and credit math (Karthik).
- Lodestar: complete vendor questionnaire and confirm preferred DocuSign signer (Theo / Procurement).
- Ops call: schedule 60-minute working session next week to align monitoring and prewarm hooks (Connor to propose times).

If that all sounds reasonable, I'll route a SOW template and the DocuSign link to procurement today.
